title: Basic Concepts of Probability and Counting

questions.prompt: The set of all possible outcomes of a probability experiment is called the:
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The sample space is the set of all possible outcomes.

questions.prompt: An event that consists of exactly one outcome is called a ___ event.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A simple event has exactly one outcome.

questions.prompt: A probability experiment consists of tossing a coin three times. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
The Fundamental Counting Principle is used to:
options: Determine the probability of an event
Find the number of ways two or more events can occur in sequence
Identify the complement of an event
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The Fundamental Counting Principle multiplies the number of ways each event can occur.

questions.prompt: An access code consists of two letters (A–Z) followed by two digits (0–9). If repetition is allowed, how many possible codes are there?
Probability based on observed data or experiments is called:
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Empirical (statistical) probability is based on observations or experiments.

questions.prompt: According to the Law of Large Numbers, as an experiment is repeated many times, the empirical probability approaches the ___ probability.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The empirical probability gets closer to the theoretical (classical) probability.
0.15 > 0.05, so it is not considered unusual.
questions.prompt: If the classical probability of an event is 0.15, is this event considered unusual? (Yes or No)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The complement $E'$ includes all outcomes not in $E$.
questions.prompt: The complement of an event $E$ is:
options: All outcomes in the sample space that are not in $E$
The sum of the probabilities of all outcomes

questions.prompt: In a survey of 500 people, 200 preferred brand A. If one person is selected at random, what is the empirical probability of preferring brand A? (Give as a simplified fraction.)
A doctor estimates a 75% chance of success for a surgery. This is an example of:
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A doctor's estimate is a subjective probability.

questions.prompt: A ___ diagram is a visual display that uses branches to show all possible outcomes of a probability experiment.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A tree diagram shows the outcomes through branches.

questions.prompt: You randomly select a number from 1 to 100. What is the classical probability of selecting a number greater than 90? (Give as a simplified fraction.)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: A probability of 0 indicates an impossible event.
